questions.q: Match each SQL keyword to what it does.
pairs: Says which table to look in
Matches part of a value using a wildcard
questions.feedback: SELECT picks columns, WHERE picks rows.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 4 — Record vault, station 3: SELECT and FROM

questions.q: Which query returns the name and form of every pupil in year 11?
options: SELECT Name, Form FROM Pupils WHERE Year = 11
SELECT Pupils FROM Name, Form WHERE Year = 11
SELECT Name, Form WHERE Pupils FROM Year = 11
questions.feedback: Fields after SELECT, table after FROM, condition after WHERE. The last option returns everything about everybody.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 4 — Record vault, station 3: SELECT and FROM

questions.q: State what is meant by a field in a database table.

markPoints.concept: one item of data held about each record, shown as a column
accept: column|category|attribute|item of data|piece of data|one piece|type of data|heading
markPoints.exemplar: One item of data held about each record, such as surname.

questions.example: A single item of data held about every record, such as the surname field — a column in the table.
questions.paraphrase: One column of the table: a single piece of information stored for each record.
questions.feedback: A field is a column; a record is a row.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 4 — Record vault, station 3: SELECT and FROM

questions.q: A table of books has a Title field. Which query finds every book whose title starts with 'The'?
options: SELECT * FROM Books WHERE Title LIKE 'The%'
SELECT * FROM Books WHERE Title LIKE '%The'
questions.feedback: The wildcard goes where the unknown part is, so 'The%' means 'starts with The'.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 4 — Record vault, station 3: SELECT and FROM
